stimuli.body:

• Exactly 5 occupied positions separate Charu and Tara in the stated order.

• Exactly 1 occupied positions separate Aditi and Bina in the stated order.

Statements: No files is a deposits. Some deposits are cheques. All cheques are accounts.
Conclusions:
I. All files are accounts.
II. Some accounts are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All files are accounts.
II. No deposits is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. Some files are not deposits.
II. No deposits is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. Some files are cheques.
II. Some deposits are accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: P > Q < R = X > T.
Conclusions: I. R > P   II. P ≥ T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
growth banking access = ze mi pa
growth rural savings = pa to ka
banking rural secure = ze ka ni
access savings secure = ni to mi
growth banking secure = ni ze pa
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: pa. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = pa, banking = ze, access = mi, rural = ka, savings = to, secure = ni.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 24 km east, turns left and walks 28 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. Net displacement is 21 km east and 28 km north. By Pythagoras, √(21² + 28²) = 35 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 33 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 57 km east, turns left and walks 44 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 55. Net displacement is 33 km east and 44 km north. By Pythagoras, √(33² + 44²) = 55 km.

questions.stem: B is the mother of D. E is the daughter of D. A is the father of D. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. A is a parent of D, and E is D’s daughter. Hence E is A’s grandchild.

questions.stem: C is the brother of D. D is the mother of F. B is the father of C and D. How is C related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of F’s mother D. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of D. D is the father of F. C is the son of F. G is the sister of D. How is D related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of F, and F is C’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 47 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 47 − 13 + 1 = 35.

questions.stem: In a queue of 41 candidates, a candidate is 9th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 29. New front rank = 9+4 = 13. Back rank = 41 − 13 + 1 = 29.

Choose the strongest relationship that holds for all possible root pairings.
options: x = y or relationship cannot be determined

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2600 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 5830.3. Recover each cost separately: 2600×100/110 + 2600×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 62 and 93 hours. An outlet empties it in 93 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 62. Net rate = 1/62 + 1/93 − 1/93 = 1/62. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 144 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 64. Still-water speed = 18 km/h. Upstream speed = 18 − 2. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 4:4. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 5 months. A receives ₹105600 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 149600. Profit ratio is 48:20. Each ratio unit = ₹2200. Total = 68 × 2200.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹28000 earns ₹12600 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 37030. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 28000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 190 litres of pure milk. 38 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 121.6. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 190 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 19 people is 36 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 56. New total minus old total = (19+1)×(36+1) − 19×36 = 56.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 17 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+17)/(x+17) = 3/2 gives x = 17. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 130 m train moving at 64.8 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 8.67. Relative speed = (64.8 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 15 m/s. Time = 130/15.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2800. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. New quantity / old quantity = 100/120. Reduction percentage = 20/120 ×100.
